[Pedagogy review · Suggestion · extension · pf-dec83b6697]
At p41-q18: Append (e) Find the area between y=e^x+e^(−x) and the x-axis for −3≤x≤3. Answer: 2(e³−e^(−3)) square units. (f) How much greater is this than the area found in part (d)? Answer: 4(1−e^(−3)) square units. (g) Explain why this difference also equals 2∫ from 0 to 3 of 2e^(−x) dx. Answer: on [0,3] the sum curve exceeds the difference curve by 2e^(−x), and each total area is twice its positive-half area.
Before the between-curves tasks beginning at p34-q8, propose a concise bridge from axis-bounded area to integrating the vertical difference between curves.
